body.prompt: Photorealistic industrial design photograph of a daily-carry aerial camera quadcopter. Orthographic 90-degree overhead, nose at twelve o'clock. True X, four motors, arms at 45 degrees to the nose axis, square hub layout, opposite hubs 250 mm apart. Four stationary propellers, each a single balanced pair of opposite equal blades, 125 mm tip to tip. Compact bevelled body, 1.6:1. At twelve o'clock a compact graphite camera with a flat smoked crown sits in a close-fitting three-sided nose recess. Two small side pivots attach it to the shell; the lens looks ahead through the vertical front face, hidden from this overhead view. Four separate arms seat flush in recessed shoulder sockets, each with one fitted collar. Tight joints and two banks of inset cooling slots. Satin warm-grey molded shell, graphite composite arms, charcoal blades. Soft 5500 K sidelight, defined contact shadows, pale seamless background. Use the four reference endpoints for motor locations. Unlettered product, full aircraft in frame. A separate U-shaped metal carrier bridges the nose cheeks around the module; leave two visible lateral pivot discs and a fitted transverse parting seam behind the carrier. Picture 2 is only the appearance of the opaque crown of a forward optical pod seen from above. Suit its housing and side supports to this brief.
